l.i: Obiect.5. Non potest arbor bona fructus malos ferre. Resp.

main_text.l: Scilicet, quatenus bona est. Si enim simpliciter bona
sit, omnes fructus eius sunt boni: id quod in vita coele-
sti futurum est: sin vero partim bona, partim mala sit,
tales etiam sunt fructus, ut in hac vita experimur.
F Dictum

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "amplectendi" (printed with a long s and t ligature, read as amplestendi) is marked [?]; "mundiciam" is uncertain (could be munditiam). The section sign before "51" is uncertain and read as §. "verae" is printed with an æ-like ligature. The "F Dictum" line at the foot is read as signature F and catchword Dictum, and the catchword is not repeated in the text. Printed "aliâs" with a circumflex is kept as printed. The "Dauid" spelling is kept as printed.
